## VIP Colombia beach holidays: how many days will you spend by the sea?

**On the current VIP Colombia beach itinerary, the main time by the water is on Barú Island: three nights at the end of a ten-day journey.** The trip first crosses the Andes and visits Cartagena, then you reach your coastal hotel by boat. No mandatory excursions are scheduled for days 8–9, giving you two full free days beside the sea between your arrival on the island and the return transfer.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The key itinerary is [Colombia VIP: Bogotá, the Coffee Region, Cartagena and Barú Island](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/). It suits travellers who want to discover the country first and then unwind for several quieter days. If your aim is to spend **the entire holiday on the beach**, much of this trip would be taken up by sightseeing transfers you do not need. You can compare other options without a VIP filter in the [Colombia beach tour catalogue](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/colombia/).

It is important to distinguish the site's VIP selection from the services that have actually been confirmed. A VIP label does not automatically mean all-inclusive board, a private yacht, an exclusive stretch of beach or daily sea excursions. This itinerary specifies hotels, private ground transfers and a boat to Barú and back. The rest depends on the stated trip conditions.

## Cartagena or Barú: where to relax

| Place | Its role in this itinerary |
|---|---|
| [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) | City, history and two hotel nights |
| [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/) | Beach finale, three nights |
| Rosario Islands | Visible along the way; no separate excursion listed |

In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the main purpose of the two-day stay is to discover the port city: walks through historic neighbourhoods, San Felipe Fortress, La Popa and everyday urban life. Sofitel Legend Santa Clara is named as the hotel for this section. It is an opportunity to experience the Caribbean coast, but it does not replace three nights at a dedicated beach destination.

[Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/) offers a different experience: proximity to the sea, free time and a change of surroundings after the excursions. The island has a variety of beaches, boat routes, mangroves and access to the region's coral ecosystems. A visit to a particular beach area or a neighbouring island needs its own itinerary unless expressly included.

The main [Colombia VIP tours page](/vip/colombia/) shows the country's options without the beach filter. The [Colombia destination guide](/colombia/) is useful if you are still deciding between the Caribbean and other regions.

## Day-by-day on Barú

### Day 7: speedboat from Cartagena and hotel check-in

After breakfast, the itinerary includes a transfer to the pier in Cartagena and a speedboat crossing of the bay towards [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/). Coastal fortifications near Bocachica and the area around the Rosario archipelago can be seen along the route. This is **a transfer to the hotel**, not a promise of a separate excursion or stops at every island along the way.

Guests are met on arrival and check in at **Las Islas**. The itinerary describes bungalow accommodation with a private pool; the exact room and any hotel substitution are confirmed when booking. Your first beach time begins after the transfer and check-in, so day 7 should not be counted as a full day beside the sea.

### Days 8–9: two free days by the Caribbean Sea

There are no mandatory excursions scheduled on these days. You can relax by the water, walk along the shore and spend time at the hotel. The description mentions possible activities: kayaking, diving, exploring mangroves and visiting Encantada Lagoon. **An activity being mentioned as a leisure option does not mean it is included in the paid package.** Boat outings, instructors, equipment and pricing must be agreed separately.

These two free days provide a chance to recover after an active itinerary. The earlier journey includes domestic flights, walks around [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), a trip to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), visits to [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), and sightseeing in Cartagena. The beach finale therefore changes the balance of activity substantially.

### Day 10: return transfer and departure

In the morning, guests travel by boat from Barú to Cartagena and then transfer to the airport. Departure time depends on the flight schedule and transport conditions. Avoid planning an extended boat excursion on day ten unless arranged separately.

Altogether, the beach portion comprises **three nights, two full free days and whatever time remains after arriving on day 7**. Travellers seeking a full week by the sea will need to agree on a different length of stay before the itinerary is confirmed.

## Caribbean Sea, mangroves and coral: possible activities

Near Barú are the protected marine ecosystems of **Corales del Rosario y de San Bernardo National Natural Park**. Colombia's national parks authority describes coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangrove forests here. They provide habitats for fish, molluscs and other marine organisms.

When choosing an additional activity, distinguish between several options:

- **An ordinary beach day.** Walks, swimming in permitted areas and relaxing at the hotel need no separate boat itinerary. Water entry conditions and waves can still change.
- **Kayaking.** This is suitable for an unhurried exploration of coastal waters when weather and local operators permit it. Confirm that a kayak and any necessary assistance are included in your rate.
- **Snorkelling or diving.** These are different activities. Scuba diving requires a licensed operator, appropriate training and compliance with rules for protected sites; these services **are not listed as included in the tour**.
- **A mangrove excursion.** The region has lagoons and coastal vegetation, but a visit to Encantada Lagoon is a potential additional trip, not a compulsory part of each day.

Coral communities are fragile: do not step on reefs, touch animals or remove shells or coral. Marine excursions in protected areas must follow the park's rules, permitted routes and restrictions relating to weather and visitor numbers.

The appearance of the sea around Barú changes with light, wind and sea conditions. Clear, calm water cannot be guaranteed from a promotional photograph. If your main interests are **wildlife, mangrove ecosystems and mountain scenery**, compare [Colombia VIP nature tours](/vip/colombia/interests/wildlife/).

## Seasons: when to combine the beach with sightseeing

The Colombian Caribbean coast has a warm climate, but sea conditions depend on wind and weather. According to the Rosario and San Bernardo national park administration, the drier season generally runs from December through April and the wetter season from May through November. This describes the region; **it is not a guarantee of sunny weather or calm seas on any particular day**.

[Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the Coffee Region have different elevations and weather patterns. Choose dates for the whole ten-day journey with both mountain excursions and the beach in mind. Sun protection and light clothing are normally useful on Barú, while warm and waterproof layers will help with early outings in the Andes.

Speedboat operations are especially dependent on conditions at sea. The marine park administration recommends using authorised operators, wearing life jackets and checking whether visits are possible. Those practical considerations matter more than promises of perfect weather along the whole route.

## What is included and what needs confirmation

The published [ten-day Colombia itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) lists hotels with breakfast, private excursions and ground transfers, admission to the specified sights, a hot-air balloon flight over the Coffee Region and **the Cartagena–Barú–Cartagena speedboat transfers**. The final three nights are scheduled at Las Islas.

Domestic flights from Bogotá to Pereira and Pereira to Cartagena, international flights, and most lunches and dinners are not on the inclusion list. Optional sea activities, visits to other islands, a separate yacht and additional hotel services are not described as part of the basic package.

| Included in the itinerary | To arrange separately |
|---|---|
| Three nights on Barú | Additional sea excursions |
| Return speedboat transfers | Diving and equipment |
| Accommodation with breakfast | Lunches and dinners |
| Tour transfers and excursions | International and domestic flights |

The tour page **does not publish a fixed price**. Comparing its cost with a beach hotel or a week-long holiday using an assumed rate would therefore be misleading. First determine the dates, the number of nights on Barú and your chosen additional activities. Only then can you prepare a comparable offer.

## Who this itinerary is for

This journey suits travellers who see the beach as an appealing conclusion to a wider introduction to Colombia. One morning you may be visiting museums and an underground cathedral in the Andes, a few days later walking among Cartagena's fortifications, and finally relaxing beside the Caribbean. Its main attraction is variety, but **it contains too much sightseeing for a holiday devoted exclusively to the sea**.

If you primarily want the shore and quiet days, choose a trip with more time on the coast from the [general Colombia beach tour catalogue](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/colombia/). If you want to combine a resort stay with museums and coffee towns, the current [ten-day Colombia VIP itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) already provides that sequence and specifies its inclusions.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many full beach days on Barú does the tour include?

Two: days 8 and 9. Three nights are scheduled on the island; day 7 includes the boat transfer and check-in, while day 10 covers the return transfer and departure.

### Does the itinerary include an excursion around the Rosario Islands?

No separate Rosario Islands excursion is listed among the inclusions. The archipelago lies in the area of the boat crossing, but a dedicated outing would need to be arranged additionally.

### Does Las Islas hotel offer all-inclusive meals as part of this tour?

The current itinerary confirms accommodation with breakfast. Full board or an all-inclusive package is not specified. The exact room and rate conditions must be established at booking.

### Can I go diving during the beach stay?

Diving is mentioned as a possible activity on Barú. It is not included among the tour's paid services. Diving arrangements, conditions and safety must be agreed separately.

### Can the stay by the sea be extended?

A private itinerary change can be discussed before booking. The published tour page does not list an automatic extension or a fixed price for extra nights.

### Is this itinerary suitable for families with children?

The children's ages, tolerance for flights, long excursions and speedboat travel need to be considered. The current itinerary does not confirm a special children's version or a separate family package, so the terms should be tailored to the specific group.

## VIP coffee tours in Colombia: from plantation to Caribbean coast

To discover authentic Colombian coffee, travel to the areas around Pereira and Salento. Green plantations stand alongside mountain valleys and small towns. Visitors can see how coffee is grown and combine a farm tour with other experiences.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. For example, [Colombia VIP: Bogotá, Coffee Region, Cartagena and Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) is a ten-day journey. Several activity-filled days in the coffee region fall between Bogotá's historic attractions and a stay beside the Caribbean Sea. It is an option for travellers who want to explore coffee culture while discovering different parts of Colombia.

## Cocora Valley, Salento and El Ocaso farm

On day four, after flying to Pereira, travellers head to the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), famous for its tall wax palms. The route continues with a walk through [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), known for its historic streets and artisan workshops.

The same day includes a separate excursion to **El Ocaso coffee farm**. This distinguishes the itinerary from a trip that only mentions coffee in restaurants or hotels. Assess the farm visit according to the actual excursion programme: its duration and activities are determined by the specific product.

Optional activities in the valley include a barista show, horse riding and separate walks. **These are listed as extras**, so they should not automatically be counted as part of the paid package. Lunch that day is also excluded from the base price.

## Hot-air balloon flight above the coffee slopes

The next day begins with an early departure for a hot-air balloon flight above plantations and green hills. The ten-day itinerary also explicitly includes a canopy activity and horse riding in the coffee valley. After a busy morning, travellers fly to Cartagena.

Balloon flights depend on weather conditions and safety requirements. Take this into account when choosing dates if the flight is one of your main reasons for travelling. Canopy activities and horse riding require a different level of physical effort from a coffee farm visit, so consider the whole day's schedule.

## Confirmed VIP services and accommodation

The [ten-day tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) lists Four Seasons Casa Medina in Bogotá, Visus Hotel Boutique & Spa in Pereira, Sofitel Legend Santa Clara in Cartagena and Las Islas on [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/). Accommodation and specific room categories are confirmed for the chosen dates.

The programme includes private transfers with a driver, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide in Bogotá and Pereira, and an English-speaking guide in Cartagena. These inclusions apply to this specific itinerary. **A VIP label alone does not guarantee that other trips will have the same hotels, guides or transport.**

Budgeting also means checking exclusions. International flights and the two domestic legs, Bogotá–Pereira and Pereira–Cartagena, are paid for separately. Certain meals and optional activities are also outside the base price.

## How to choose a coffee journey

One substantial farm visit offers an introduction to the origins of coffee beans. A journey devoted to professional coffee study, however, may feature several farms, different processing methods, roasting and extended tastings. These are distinct formats.

The main idea of this programme is to bring together a coffee farm, [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and several days by the [Caribbean Sea](/colombia/place/baru-island/). For a more specialised focus, compare [general coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/) and [trips around Colombia](/colombia/tour/).

Useful questions before booking include whether you will visit a working estate, the guide's language, how much time is spent at the farm versus other stops, and which services cost extra. A route through different climate zones calls for clothing suitable both for cool mornings in the Andes and for the warm coast.

## Frequently asked questions about VIP coffee tours in Colombia

### Is a visit to a real coffee farm included?

Yes. The [ten-day VIP itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) includes a separate excursion to El Ocaso.

### Is there an overnight stay in the coffee region?

Yes, in Pereira, before the hot-air balloon flight and the onward journey to Cartagena.

### Is the barista show included in the price?

It is an optional activity. Its cost and content must be agreed separately.

### Can coffee experiences be combined with a beach holiday?

Yes. The route ends on [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/), with several days free from a packed sightseeing schedule.

### Which extra costs should be considered?

These include domestic and international flights, some meals and optional activities. The final cost depends on the dates and confirmed inclusions.

## VIP culture and history tours in Colombia: route and experiences

**For discovering Colombia's history, three parts of the current VIP itinerary are particularly important: Bogotá, the area around the capital and Cartagena.** First come pre-Columbian artefacts and historic quarters, followed by the sacred lake of the Muisca people and an underground salt cathedral, and finally a fortified Caribbean port. Between them lie the coffee towns of the Andes, where culture is closely linked to everyday rural life.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The main current itinerary is [Colombia VIP: Bogotá, Coffee Region, Cartagena and Barú Island, 10 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/). It includes city excursions, some admission tickets, named hotels and private transfers. **This is a specific journey with a cultural component, not a promise of any excursion in the country on demand.**

A VIP classification alone does not establish the guide's language, group size or category of every hotel. This particular product confirms private excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Bogotá and Pereira, while Cartagena sightseeing is accompanied by an English-speaking guide. To compare all cultural itineraries, including options beyond the VIP filter, visit the [Colombia culture and history tour catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/).

## Cultural experiences by region: what you visit and when

| Area | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) | Gold Museum, Botero and La Candelaria |
| [Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) | Muisca heritage and the El Dorado legend |
| [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) | Underground Salt Cathedral |
| [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) | Coffee culture and crafts |
| [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) | Colonial neighbourhoods and fortresses |

Within the ten-day trip, three nights are spent in Bogotá, one in Pereira, two in Cartagena and the final three on Barú Island. This helps set expectations: historical sightseeing is concentrated at the beginning and in the middle, with a more relaxed finale. Ten days **do not mean ten days of museums or private excursions**.

## Bogotá: pre-Columbian gold, art and urban history

The first full sightseeing day in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) introduces the historic district of La Candelaria. Colonial homes stand alongside civic institutions, museums and university buildings. The itinerary includes Plaza de Bolívar and the main monuments around it. Visitors then head to Monserrate, with views over the city and its high-altitude plateau.

### The Gold Museum and Indigenous heritage

The Banco de la República Gold Museum displays archaeological objects from pre-Columbian cultures. **The value of a visit lies not only in seeing ornaments, but in understanding the role of gold in rituals and beliefs among different peoples.** This cultural context connects the exhibits with the region's history before Spanish conquest. The itinerary provides a private guide for Bogotá sightseeing.

Later, the route continues to Casa de la Moneda, where money and coinage are explored alongside Colombian history, and the Botero Museum, dedicated to painting, graphic art and sculpture. These visits span different periods, from pre-Columbian art to Colombia's modern artistic traditions.

Check museum opening schedules when selecting dates. The Gold Museum's official rules confirm that it is closed on Mondays. The current tour description also specifies that the Botero Museum and Casa de la Moneda are closed on Tuesdays. Visits are coordinated with the calendar; mechanically assigning every museum to a fixed weekday could be a mistake.

### Monserrate and a view of the capital

Ascending Monserrate adds geographical context to the historical walk: Bogotá stands at approximately 2,600 metres above sea level. From above, it becomes easier to understand how the city expanded along the Andean plateau and how its older districts connect with modern development. A sudden change in altitude after arriving from lower regions can be noticeable, so the intensity of the first excursion should reflect how you feel.

## Guatavita and Zipaquirá: rituals, salt and legends

The next dedicated sightseeing day brings together two different stories. [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) is known for its connection with Muisca rituals, while [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) is associated with the industrial and religious heritage of salt mining.

### From a sacred lake to the El Dorado legend

Guatavita is linked to Muisca beliefs about authority, ceremonies and sacred places. The later European legend of El Dorado grew from accounts of gold and the initiation ritual of a ruler. **It is useful to distinguish historical information about Muisca culture from later tales of a mythical city of gold.** The journey lets you hear this story close to the lake and walk along mountain trails.

The whole outing, including travel, is allocated around nine hours. According to the itinerary, the lake is closed to visitors on Mondays. Lunch that day is paid for separately, so the excursion is not an all-inclusive package.

### Zipaquirá Salt Cathedral

The Catedral de Sal lies approximately 180 metres below ground in former salt workings. It is notable for the combination of mining history, architecture and Catholic symbolism. Underground passages and illuminated chambers create a very different impression from churches above ground.

After visiting the town and the cathedral, the route returns to Bogotá. If mining or architecture interests you, time spent here may be more valuable than another general sightseeing stop in the capital. A separate technical tour of the mines, which is not in the itinerary, must not be counted as included.

## Coffee Region: living culture beyond museums

On day four, the route moves on to [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). Here history is seen less in museum galleries than in the layout of settlements, farms, artisan workshops and coffee traditions.

Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2011. Its significance is linked to generations of small farmers cultivating mountain slopes and to the architecture of Andean settlements. This is a regional tradition, not a single museum with a fixed route through its rooms.

In [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), the programme includes a walk through the streets and an introduction to local workshops. A separate [El Ocaso coffee farm excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) offers a look at the journey from coffee cherry to cup. Such a visit is valuable for anyone interested in working culture and local production methods.

After the main sightseeing programme, optional activities include a barista show or horseback riding. Their terms and prices are agreed separately. The words "Coffee Region" in an itinerary do not mean every tasting workshop is included.

## Cartagena: fortified port and historic neighbourhoods

The cultural and historical part of the tour culminates in [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Its port, fortresses and group of monuments form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city's historical importance is bound up with Caribbean trade routes and a defensive system developed by the Spanish colonial administration from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century.

The confirmed excursion includes La Popa hill and its Santa Cruz monastery, San Felipe de Barajas fortress, the old defensive walls and the historic centre. It also takes in Getsemaní and Las Bóvedas. The latter is particularly interesting as an example of former military and storage spaces given new uses within the modern city.

**Cartagena and Bogotá differ in the very subject of their sightseeing.** In the capital, museums and pre-Columbian heritage take centre stage; here the focus is a fortified port, defensive architecture, colonial buildings and everyday life in coastal neighbourhoods. An English-speaking guide is specified for Cartagena. If a Russian-speaking guide throughout the entire trip is essential, do not assume this is included simply because Russian is used on other sections.

After Cartagena, the itinerary includes three nights on [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/) beside the sea. It is a natural conclusion to an intensive cultural programme, but details of the beach stay are covered by the [Colombia VIP beach selection](/vip/colombia/interests/beach-holidays/), rather than by the history of fortresses and museums.

## Choosing the format and understanding inclusions

The [ten-day itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) lists private transfers, accommodation with breakfast, tickets to scheduled sights, private excursions and guides in the specified languages. The named hotels are Four Seasons Casa Medina, Visus Hotel Boutique & Spa, Sofitel Legend Santa Clara and Las Islas. Under the trip conditions, hotels may be replaced with others of the same category.

The cost excludes international flights and the domestic Bogotá–Pereira and Pereira–Cartagena flights. Lunches, dinners and certain optional activities are not automatically included either. No fixed price is shown on the published page, so numerical rate comparisons are impossible without a confirmed offer.

The selection suits travellers wanting **a structured introduction to Colombian history** while keeping a few days for nature, coffee and the sea. For a deeper exploration of one period, choose a more focused route with additional time in Bogotá or Cartagena. You can search for these in the [general Colombia culture and history tour catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) without restricting the choice to VIP tours.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which matters more for Colombian history: Bogotá or Cartagena?

Bogotá's main themes are pre-Columbian collections, museums and the development of the capital. Cartagena is better suited to understanding colonial trade, architecture and fortifications. The current itinerary visits both cities.

### Can I visit the Gold Museum on a Monday?

According to the published schedule of the Gold Museum in Bogotá, it is closed on Mondays. The itinerary is planned around museum opening days. Current opening hours are checked immediately before travel.

### What languages are used for cultural excursions?

The published itinerary specifies private excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Bogotá and Pereira, and an English-speaking guide in Cartagena. Russian-language guiding throughout all ten days is not promised on the tour page.

### Does the trip cover the entire Coffee Region?

The itinerary includes specific stops in Pereira, Salento, Cocora Valley and at a coffee farm. It does not cover every town or estate in the Coffee Region. Visiting more would require a separate itinerary and quote.

### How is this VIP selection different from Colombia's general excursion catalogue?

This selection contains tours at the intersection of Colombia, the culture theme and the VIP filter. [Colombia excursions](/colombia/excursion/) are separate products, not necessarily the entire ten-day route with accommodation and transfers.

## VIP food and wine tours in Colombia: what is included

**The principal culinary experience in this VIP selection is a coffee farm visit explaining production and including a tasting.** Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The itinerary brings together the capital's culture, the coffee-growing Andes and the Caribbean coast. The designated coffee day takes place near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) and [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/).

This is a combined journey. Unlike a specialist culinary route with several producers and tasting dinners, coffee occupies an important but limited part of the trip. The main tour in this selection is [Colombia VIP: Bogotá, Coffee Region, Cartagena and Barú Island](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/). For comparison with other tours on the same theme, see [Colombia food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/colombia/) and [dedicated coffee routes](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/).

## El Ocaso coffee farm: from cherry to cup

Colombia's Coffee Region combines mountain slopes, farms and small towns. The country's Coffee Cultural Landscape has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2011. Its value is tied to traditions of growing coffee on challenging mountain terrain, the lives of farming families and the architecture of the settlements.

The current itinerary includes an [El Ocaso coffee farm excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/). A local expert demonstrates coffee cultivation, hand-picking the cherries, processing, drying and roasting the beans. Guests taste freshly brewed coffee, and coffee lemonade is served at the end. This is the specific content of a standalone excursion, which you can review before choosing the whole trip.

The same day covers the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/) and its wax palms, as well as a walk through Salento. This sequence lets you discover not only the drink in your cup but also the landscapes, farms and local life. The [El Ocaso coffee farm page](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/) provides details about the location itself. Visits to additional estates must be arranged as extras rather than assumed to be included.

## Ten days: combining food, history and beaches

The route lasts ten days and nine nights. Its sections have different themes and travel arrangements.

| Area | Main programme |
|---|---|
| [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), 3 nights | Museums, Monserrate, Guatavita and Zipaquirá |
| [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), 1 night | Cocora, Salento and El Ocaso farm |
| [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), 2 nights | Old town, fortress and historic neighbourhoods |
| [Barú](/colombia/place/baru-island/), 3 nights | Caribbean Sea and island relaxation |

In Bogotá, private sightseeing visits museums and historic places. After flying to Pereira, travellers explore the coffee farm and Cocora Valley; the following morning they take a hot-air balloon flight over coffee plantations. The journey then continues in Cartagena and ends with several nights on Barú Island.

**This balance is the deciding factor when choosing a culinary itinerary.** If you want to understand coffee processing and visit one working estate, the experience fits well within a broader trip. If your goal is several days of tastings, comparisons between farms and training in coffee preparation, you should discuss a different programme.
